profiles.profile: T1: gross R30 000, pension R3 000 a month, two-person medical aid

cases.question: Which tax bracket am I in?
cases.reply: Your taxable income for the year is R 324 000,00. That puts you in the 26% bracket, which covers income above R 245 100 up to R 383 100. Only the part of your income inside that bracket, R 78 900,00, is taxed at 26%. After rebates and credits, your tax for the year is R 37 788,00.

cases.question: How much would an RA save me?
cases.reply: Your retirement contributions already save you about R 780,00 a month (R 9 360,00 a year). As an example, R 1 000 more a month would cut your tax by about R 260,00 a month (R 3 120,00 a year). That is an illustration from your own figures, not advice.

cases.question: Why is my take-home pay lower than my salary?
cases.reply: Your gross pay is R 30 000,00 a month. PAYE of R 3 149,00, UIF of R 177,12 and your retirement contribution of R 3 000,00 come off, which leaves R 23 673,88 in your bank account.

cases.question: What would happen if I got a R10 000 bonus?
cases.reply: A bonus of R 10 000,00 would be taxed at your top rate of 26%, so about R 2 600,00 would go in tax and you would keep R 7 400,00.

cases.question: How much tax do I pay in a year?
cases.reply: Your tax for the year is about R 37 800.

cases.question: Why is my PAYE what it is?
cases.reply: Your PAYE in a normal month is R 3 149,00. Over a whole year your tax is R 37 788,00 after the primary rebate of R 17 820,00 and your medical aid credit of R 9 024,00. I don't have a figure for what each month's share of that is beyond the PAYE above.

cases.question: What is my retirement limit?
cases.reply: The most SARS lets you deduct for retirement saving is R 350 000,00 a year.
